faq.q: Can I make beauty ads from one product photo?
faq.a: Yes. Upload a clear, straight-on photo or paste a product link, then describe a routine, swatch, unboxing, or review-style clip. Compare the shade and the package with the real item before you post.

faq.q: Can I make a before-and-after of skin results?
faq.a: No. A generated face is not evidence of what a product does to skin. Show application, texture, and packaging, and keep result claims out of the ad.

faq.q: Will the clip match my foundation or lipstick shade?
faq.a: Color follows your photo and your wording. Shoot in daylight and name the shade in plain words, such as warm beige liquid. If the tone drifts, make another version. Credits for a failed job come back.

faq.q: Can I put a price or a promo code on the image?
faq.a: Prices, codes, and shade names are safer typed by you. Voice and captions come with the clip, and you can fix them in the editor before download.

faq.q: What photo should I upload for skincare?
faq.a: Use a straight-on shot, label toward the camera, on a plain surface, with no hands in frame. Glossy tubes and glass pick up glare, so use window light instead of flash.

faq.q: How long should a beauty ad be, and what does it cost?
faq.a: Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. A 6-second clip is 24 credits, 10 seconds is 40, 15 seconds is 60, and 30 seconds is 120. Use a short length for one pump or swatch.

faq.q: Can I run the clips as paid beauty ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloads are watermark-free and licensed for commercial use, including paid ads. Keep ingredient and result claims accurate, and add text in your editor so you can check it.

faq.q: How is this different from hiring a creator?
faq.a: You upload one photo or paste a link, pick a generated presenter, and pay the credits shown before the job, instead of a creator fee and revision rounds. Present the clip as an ad, not as a customer's review.

faq.q: Does the beauty clip include a voice and captions?
faq.a: Yes. The job can include a spoken line and captions, and you can fix both in the editor before you download. A failed job returns its credits.
